correctness.rationale: For N>=2 prescribed positive reduced gravities, H>0 and positive depths summing to H, the rigid-lid generalized Jacobi eigenproblem is exactly K(h)eta=c^-2 D eta. With a_j=1/g_j and alternating v_j=(-1)^(j-1)a_j, v^T D v=S and sum |v_j-v_{j-1}|=2S. The Rayleigh bound and weighted Cauchy–Schwarz show lambda_max>=4S/H, with equality only for h_i=H(a_{i-1}+a_i)/(2S). At those depths K(h*)v=(4S/H)Dv; sign-conjugation produces a positive Perron vector of the tridiagonal matrix, making that eigenvalue the largest and proving attainability. N=2 scalar boundary holds; N=3 trace gives 1:2 slow/fast squared-speed ratio. Fresh generalized-eigenproblem calculations tested 325 randomized depth/gravity choices across N=2..14; universal proof is analytic.
residual_risks: Hydrostatic long-wave, rigid-lid Boussinesq, zero current/rotation, gravities fixed and independent of depth; no finite-wavelength or nonlinear assertion.

evidence: Both primary physical papers address modal eigenvalues for specified layer thicknesses; the 2019 author manuscript examines three layers, without inspected all-N global allocation
broader_coverage.reasoning: Known eigenmode formulas do not automatically entail an exact global optimizer with uniqueness and arbitrary jumps. Generic matrix inequalities provide tools but require a tailored alternating test vector.

originality.rationale: The physical multilayer eigenproblem and modal orthogonality are classical, including Shimizu (2011) and de Melo Viríssimo–Milewski (2019), but the inspected fixed-geometry mode theory does not itself state a unique global optimizer for the smallest speed over every fixed-total-depth allocation and arbitrary positive buoyancy jumps. The all-N inverse-gravity adjacent-depth rule is the assessed theorem, not generic Cauchy–Schwarz or two-layer equal-depth folklore. Shimizu publisher full text was not fully accessible and Oxford authorized access returned VPN disconnected; do not infer complete exclusion.

value.rationale: The output is an exact, unique allocation rule with physically interpretable inverse-buoyancy weights, valid for arbitrary numbers of layers and independent positive jumps. Maximizing the slowest mode under total-depth resource constraint is a natural optimal-stratification question; N=3 half-depth middle-layer law is a nontrivial concrete consequence, not a parameter renaming.
residual_risks: The discovery is long-wave linear hydrostatic mode optimization, not a claim about real ocean profiles with coupled density/depth dynamics.
